long_biography.plain_text:
Brooklyn-born Robert W. Firestone entered Syracuse University at sixteen and later trained in psychology at Berkeley, Los Angeles and Denver. Work with people experiencing schizophrenia shaped the theory he developed around self-destructive thought and emotional defences. He established a private practice in Los Angeles, then withdrew from clinical work in 1979 to focus on research, writing and art. His Brooklyn upbringing as the son of a physician and fashion designer supplies no documented link to the industrial Firestone family's holdings.

As consulting theorist to the Glendon Association, Firestone developed Separation Theory, Voice Therapy and assessment tools addressing suicide and violence. His output included books, research articles, educational films and paintings. That professional record identifies income-producing practice and intellectual work, but it does not disclose a principal private company, investment portfolio or ownership stake from which personal wealth can be classified. Firestone died in Santa Barbara in 2024.
